nodes.name: Ru aerogel synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ru hydrogel was synthesized as detailed in the experimental section (not provided in main text), followed by freeze-drying to obtain Ru aerogel.
nodes.source_text: The CeO2-Ru aerogel was prepared by anchoring CeO2 QDs onto the as-synthesized Ru hydrogel, followed by freeze-drying to obtain CeO2-Ru aerogel, as detailed described in the experimental section and Figure 1a.

nodes.name: CeO2-Ru aerogels synthesis (various ratios)
nodes.procedure: CeO2-Ru aerogels with different mass ratios (namely, 1:5, 1:1, and 3:1, labeled as CeO2-Ru(1-5), CeO2-Ru(1-1), and CeO2-Ru(3-1)) were synthesized by the similar method of anchoring CeO2 QDs onto Ru aerogel followed by freeze-drying.

unit_operations.name: CeO2 QDs anchoring
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: anchoring CeO2 QDs onto the as-synthesized Ru hydrogel through interfacial Ru-O-Ce bridge

unit_operations.name: Freeze-drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: followed by freeze-drying to obtain CeO2-Ru aerogel

nodes.source_text: The CeO2-Ru aerogel was prepared by anchoring CeO2 QDs onto the as-synthesized Ru hydrogel... nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Ru aerogel with affluent porous structure providing sites for uniform CeO2 QDs loading on CeO2-Ru aerogel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As given in Figure S2a ... The Ru aerogel exhibited affluent porous structure to provide abundant active sites for the uniform loading of CeO2 QDs (Figure S2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms Ru nanoparticles of 5.9±0.1 nm self-assembled into networks for Ru aerogel; CeO2-Ru aerogel preserves porous structure with uniform CeO2 QDs dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical TEM images of the Ru aerogel was displayed (Figure S2b), confirming the self-assembling of Ru nanoparticles (NPs) with size of 5.9±0.1 nm ... SEM and TEM images (Figure 1b,c) displayed the well preservation of the porous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.234 and 0.206 nm for Ru (100) and (101) planes in Ru aerogel; 0.312 and 0.234 nm for Ru (100) and CeO2 (111) planes with close contact in CeO2-Ru aerogel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacings of 0.234 and 0.206 nm in the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image for Ru aerogel were respectively attributed to the (100) and (101) planes ... The lattice spacings of 0.312 and 0.234 nm were indexed to Ru (100) and CeO2 (111) planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED confirms polycrystalline structure for Ru aerogel and diffraction rings for (111),(222) CeO2 and (100),(101) Ru planes in CeO2-Ru aerogel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern also exhibited the polycrystalline structure for Ru aerogel ... The insert SAED pattern in Figure 1d showed the diffraction rings belonging to the (111) and (222) planes of CeO2 and those indexing to (100) and (101) planes of Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and elemental mapping confirm uniform distribution of CeO2 QDs on Ru aerogel surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annual dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image, and corresponding elemental mapping images affirmed the uniform distribution of CeO2 QDs on the surface of Ru aerogel.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen physisorption shows specific surface areas of 40.59 m²g⁻¹ for Ru aerogel and 40.44 m²g⁻¹ for CeO2-Ru aerogel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen physisorption isotherms based on Brunauer-Emmet-Teller (BET) method revealed that the specific surface areas of Ru aerogel and CeO2-Ru aerogel were 40.59 and 40.44 m²g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows mixture phase with lower crystallinity for CeO2-Ru aerogel; peaks at 38.4°, 42.2°, 44.0°, 58.3°, 69.4°, 78.4° for Ru (100),(002),(101),(102),(110),(103) planes and RuO2; CeO2 peaks at 28.5°, 47.6°, 56.3°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern was employed ... the introduction of CeO2 QDs significantly regulated the crystal phase and crystallinity of Ru aerogel, leading to the mixture phase and lower crystallinity for CeO2-Ru aerogel.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows peaks at ≈511 and 623 cm⁻¹ for RuO2 Eg and A1g modes in Ru aerogel; ≈461 cm⁻¹ for CeO2 F2g mode confirming presence of both Ru and CeO2 in CeO2-Ru aerogel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra was also utilized ... the peaks appeared ≈511 and 623 cm⁻¹ were attributed to the characteristic bending (Eg) and stretching (A1g) vibration modes for RuO2 ... at ≈461 cm⁻¹ was attributed to the symmetric stretching vibrational mode (F2g) of the CeO2 fluorite phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ru 3p metallic Ru at 462.0/484.3 eV and Ru4+ at 464.6/487.1 eV with ~0.1 eV positive shift in CeO2-Ru vs Ru aerogel; Ce 3d Ce3+/Ce4+ peaks shifted +0.2 eV; O 1s lattice oxygen reduced by 0.4 eV confirming Ru-O-Ce electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ru 3p spectra (Figure 2d), the peaks appeared at 462.0 and 484.3 eV corresponded to the metallic Ru species ... CeO2-Ru aerogel exhibited a positive shift of ≈0.1 eV ... the peaks in CeO2-Ru aerogel corresponding to Ce3+ and Ce4+ ... showed the positive shift of 0.2 eV ... lattice oxygen peak in the CeO2-Ru aerogel was significantly reduced by 0.4 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows enhanced H-O-H bending at 1630 cm⁻¹ and O-H stretching at 3235/3420 cm⁻¹ for CeO2-Ru aerogel vs Ru aerogel, confirming faster water dissociation at Ru-O-Ce interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast to Ru aerogel, the bending vibration peak of H-O-H for CeO2-Ru aerogel displayed the significant enhancement and rapid attenuation ... indicating the effective acceleration of water dissociation ... the intensity of the O-H stretching vibration signals ... notably increased for CeO2-Ru aerogel.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando ATR-SEIRAS shows stronger δ(H-O-H) at ~1600 cm⁻¹ and ν(O-H) 2900-3700 cm⁻¹ peaks for CeO2-Ru aerogel vs Ru, indicating more free water molecules at Ru-O-Ce interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with Ru aerogel, the stronger δ(H-O-H) and ν(O-H) peaks for CeO2-Ru aerogel indicate more free water molecules to approach the active sites ... at the Ru-O-Ce interface.
